question: Which of the following dynasties arose as a result of Alexander’s invasion?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maurya **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mauryan dynasty arose as a result of Alexander's invasion of India**
 
• The **Nanda dynasty ruled over North India **when Alexander invaded in 326 BCE.
 
• The last ruler of the **Nanda dynasty was Dhana Nanda.**
 
• Chandragupta Maurya overthrew **Dhana Nanda and laid the foundation for the Mauryan dynasty.**
 
• **Alexander's invasion of India also had an indirect effect on the rise of the Yavana power in Bactria, which ruled for over a century. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pandya Dynasty****​**

 
 
• The Pandya kingdom was a Tamil kingdom in south India.
 
• Madurai __was the capital of the__ Pandyan dynasty__ until the middle of the 14th century and __Korkai __was also the__ capital and port city of Pandya.__
 
• The third capital was Tenkasi until the end of the 16th century.
 
• The Pandyas revived under Kadungon (590 – 620 CE) towards the end of the 6th century, helped to disestablish the Kalabhras in south India.
 
 
 
• **Chalukya Dynasty**
 
 
• ​Pulakeshin I established the Chalukya dynasty in 543.
 
• Pulakeshin I took Vatapi (modern Badami in Bagalkot district, Karnataka) under his control and made it his capital.
 
• "Chalukyas of Badami" is how Pulakeshin I and his descendants are known.
 
• They ruled over an empire that comprised the entire state of Karnataka and most of Andhra Pradesh in the Deccan.
 
 
 
• **Pallava Dynasty****​**
 
 
• Kalabhara rule for 250 years after Sangam Age in Tamil country.
 
• The Pallava dynasty situated in Tondaimandalam and capital at Kanchipuram.
 
• Source of Pallava was disputed while many consider them to natives.
 
• They Issued earlier inscriptions in Sanskrit & Prakrit & patronized Brahmanism.
 
• Samundragupta defeated to Vishnugopa in his Southern expedition.
